text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Committee proposes restricting supermarket construction, and trend that makes daily goods shopping less available to people without cars.
- Justice Minister Kari Hakamies and supreme court president Olavi Heinonen want to limit supreme court judges' arbitration assignments which give them significant incomes. @

- Finland appealing to Russia to free Uzbekistani writer and human rights activist Albert Mussin who was arrested in Moscow on Monday to be extradited to Uzbekistan before he could come to Finland for a year's refuge.
- Finland will not accept EU proposal for cutting carbon dioxide emissions by 10 percent by 2010 compared to 1990.
- Chinese aplite stone not suitable replacement material for Finlandia Hall's crumbling marble walls, City of Helsinki committee says. @
- Merita's top managers would earn millions through their options scheme if Merita shares rise in line with analysts' expectations.
KAUPPALEHTI
- A special tax unit to be set up for the 100 largest companies and their subsidiaries.
- Savings banks have received half a billion markka in hidden bank support, cooperative banks say. @
AAMULEHTI

- Estonia disaster investigators have found that the events happened faster than earlier estimated, and that Captain Arvo Andresson arrived at the navigating bridge some 15 minutes before start of emergency situation.
- Police may have to lay off staff due to a lack of money.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Roadworks can cause accidents which are often more serious than average crashes. @
- Banks have lost private car financing to specialised financing companies, part of which belong to banking groups but others are owned by car importers.
- Sawn goods export markets are so strong that sawmills cannot meet demand, but on the other hand there are no buyers for their by-products due to uncertain pulp markets.
DEMARI
- Finns are active workers but therefore retire earlier than their Nordic counterparts, study shows.
- Paper workers union may press for separate sector pay deals in talks this autumn, chairman Jarmo Lahteenmaki says. @
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Four companies -- Sanoma Oy, Janton Oy, Metro International and Estopress -- competing to publish Metro which will be distributed freely in public transport.
